resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give a 40-foot pole L-4 tower in 1952; the Forest Lookouts page gives a 50-foot tower with a 14x14 cab for the same year. The story reports both.
firelookout.com gives four miles west of Northport; the Forest Lookouts page gives five miles. The story reports both.

The National Historic Lookout Register gives 4,187 ft (1,276 m); the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register gives 4,255 ft (1,297 m). The story reports both; the record keeps the register figure, 1276.2 m, from the original Flagstaff entry.

The register, firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page describe the cab being moved to Northport. The Association's Washington list shows a standing tower at Northport, and the 2013 report says the lookout is in a town park. The sources do not say whether the tower or only the cab was re-erected.

The 2011 report calls the lookout abandoned for cell towers and Northport working to move it. The 2013 reports and the register say it was taken down and the cab moved. The story gives both as sequence, not as a conflict.

notes_for_editor: Reads: NHLR, Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts page, both Association chapter-report PDFs (six reads). The Association's Washington list was reused from the Deming pass. No WebSearch used. Record checks: county Stevens, coordinates (FFA list) and standing status match. Sibling record flag, not a correction to this one: us-wa-flagstaff has height_m 15.2 (50 feet), which matches the 1952 tower on the Forest Lookouts page, not the 40-foot 1971 DNR tower that was dismantled in 2013. That sibling record also lists status relocated while the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register lists the site as gone, and its conflicts list records the NHLR as showing it standing when registered. Whoever edits that record should check these. Whether the tower or only the cab was re-erected in Northport is unresolved in the sources; the story says so. Access 'public' rests on the town-park placement; no hours or climbing rules were found. The 2011 report's broken word in 'Department ofNatural' is avoided in the quotes.
